entities.name: Eric V of Denmark
entities.label: Person
entities.summary: Eric V Klipping was King of Denmark from 1259 to 1286. After his father Christopher I died, his mother Margaret Sambiria ruled Denmark in his name until 1266, proving to be a competent regent. Between 1261 and 1262, the young King Eric was a prisoner in Holstein following a military defeat. Afterwards, he lived in Brandenburg, where he was initially held captive by John I, Margrave of Brandenburg. During his reign, he enforced his power successfully over the church but failed to do so on the nobility, he offended the nobles and was thereby forced to accept a charter (Håndfæstning) which limited his authority while confirming the rights of the nobles.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Eric V Klipping's reign was marked by a failed attempt to limit nobility power through the Håndfæstning charter, which had significant regional impact on Danish politics.
